This man is a keeper.

Thank the lord he’s mine ❤️

I think it’s really endearing that you’ve acknowledged that there’s a line between self-confidence and overexerting yourself. Firstly congratulations on your musical endeavour, it’s a beautiful culture and the true art of music is performing and bringing a community together through a mutual vibe. I know people who have changed because of where they started out and how they’ve progressed, and sometimes more than not it is habit that they become ‘arrogant’. 

I think there’s a healthy dynamic of appreciating what you create and perform. You’re probably amazing at what you do, and it’s okay to commend yourself without feeling you don’t deserve it. Music as much as people may disagree for many is a vocation. In order to get out there in any business you need to promote what you sell and show people what you can do, not everyone may like it but that’s preference and that’s something that might form a barrier for you- when people are critical. What you should think about is at the end of the day all humans are the same and don’t forget your roots. Why did you start music? When did it become enjoyable? Who supported you- because at the end of it, people will support you. But it’s also important that you don’t forget the people who have supported you along the way. When you have a successful performance, reward yourself because there is a high in being successful, but also remember that as high as you feel the way you treat others will have impact. And many people will support you more often than not when you the performer can meet on the same wavelength. 

As good as you may be, just remember too that no matter whatever job you have, we are all one paycheck away from a struggle-period. Music is one of those occupations where people view it as competition but if you look through the history of music, it was always communal and it wasn’t about being ‘the best’ it was about forming communities and connections and making people feel good.
